title: Log cabin square — four colour
subtitle: A different colour in each of the four strip quadrants for a patchwork effect
excerpt: Four colours, one per quadrant, make the log cabin square read like a patchwork block. Each set of two strips that form a quadrant uses one colour; the result is a square divided into four distinct colour areas meeting at the centre rectangle.
sourceNotes: Log cabin patchwork with four-colour quadrants: documented in American quilting manuals from the 1880s. The crochet strip-construction equivalent follows the same geometry.
heroPrompt: A four-colour log cabin crochet square in sage, terracotta, mustard, and cream DK cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Four distinct colour quadrants radiate from a cream centre rectangle.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished square measures 12 × 12 cm in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Log cabin square — four colour
chartDefinition.caption: Centre in colour A. Each quadrant pair of strips uses a different colour: B (right), C (top), D (left), repeat with A (bottom).

glossaryTerms.definition: In a four-colour log cabin square, each pair of opposite strips forms one quadrant. One colour per quadrant keeps the four areas visually distinct.

content.text: sequence turn the log cabin square into a patchwork block. Each colour works two strips — one horizontal and one vertical — so the four areas share a corner at the centre rectangle.
Work the centre rectangle in a neutral, then proceed with one colour per quadrant pair. Fasten off cleanly after each pair and weave in as you go to keep the wrong side tidy.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 3 g each of four DK-weight cotton colours. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle and scissors.

content.text: Work the centre rectangle in colour A (4 rows, 6 sts wide). Attach colour B and work 2 strips along the right side. Rotate 90 degrees, attach colour C, work 2 strips along the top. Continue with colour D for the left side and colour A again for the bottom to complete the first complete ring of quadrant strips. Repeat for a larger block, or fasten off for the 12 cm size.
Try the textured log cabin, which uses htr and bobble rows alongside dc strips. Or move to the bavarian crochet square for a totally different approach to coloured concentric squares.
